stem: An adult with primary hypothyroidism has a levothyroxine dose change. Which plan best evaluates the response to the new dose?

options.A: Adjust the dose each day according to symptoms alone.
options.B: Repeat serum TSH the next day and retitrate immediately.
options.C: Stop laboratory monitoring once levothyroxine therapy has begun.
options.D: Reassess clinically and measure serum TSH after about 6 to 8 weeks.

rationale: Current levothyroxine labeling recommends periodic laboratory testing together with clinical evaluation. In adults with primary hypothyroidism, serum TSH should be monitored 6 to 8 weeks after any dosage change. Therefore D is correct.
educational_objective: Apply appropriate TSH monitoring timing after levothyroxine dose changes in adults with primary hypothyroidism.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
source_locator: Dosage and Administration 2.4 — Monitoring TSH and/or Thyroxine (T4) Levels; Adults
source_claim_supported: In adults with primary hypothyroidism, adequacy of levothyroxine therapy is assessed with clinical evaluation and laboratory testing; serum TSH is monitored 6 to 8 weeks after a dosage change.

correction_summary: Replaced the secondary ATA source with current DailyMed labeling per the pharmacology source hierarchy; specified adult primary hypothyroidism to avoid central-hypothyroidism ambiguity; converted the item to an exact label-supported monitoring question and reduced difficulty from hard to easy.
audit_findings: DailyMed section 2.4 directly supports D for adults with primary hypothyroidism. A, B and C conflict with label-recommended clinical/laboratory monitoring. The primary-hypothyroidism qualifier excludes inappropriate generalization to central hypothyroidism. Independent second pass confirmed D is uniquely correct.
